original_question: Does there exist any surface in the standard 3-sphere S^3 whose position vector is of finite k-type for some finite integer k greater than 2?
target_in_paper: §2.2, especially the sentence immediately preceding Conjecture 2 asserting that there should be no surfaces of k-type in S^3 for any finite k>2; the nearest labeled formulation is Conjecture 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient 3-sphere, asks the right existence/nonexistence question, and focuses on the k>2 regime that the paper isolates immediately before stating Conjecture 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
missing_details: The paper’s notion of finite k-type is extrinsic: one studies the E^4-valued immersion x:M→S^3⊂E^4, not an intrinsic 'position vector in S^3'. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

The surface should be presented as a connected immersed surface M^2 with the metric induced from the ambient Euclidean space, and Δ is the Laplace-Beltrami operator of that induced metric. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

To be of finite k-type in the paper’s sense, x must admit a spectral decomposition x=c+x1+⋯+xk with c a constant vector in E^4 and each xi a nonconstant E^4-valued map satisfying Δxi=λi xi. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
The eigenvalues λ1,…,λk must be mutually distinct for the surface to be called k-type, and 'finite type' by itself is broader than 'k-type'. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

The nearest official paper formulation is broader than the draft: Conjecture 2 classifies all finite type surfaces in the standardly embedded S^3 as minimal surfaces, standard 2-spheres, or products of plane circles. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

Nearby context explains why the broader conjecture packages the lower-type cases: §1 recalls the 1-type characterization, and §3.1 recalls that 2-type surfaces in S^3 are the products of two plane circles, with the classification local as well. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

No algebraic choices such as base field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are part of this problem; the missing stand-alone data are the immersion, ambient Euclidean space, induced Laplacian, and spectral-decomposition conditions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
refined_question: Let x:M^2→S^3⊂E^4 be a connected immersed surface in the standard 3-sphere, viewed as an E^4-valued immersion, and let Δ be the Laplace-Beltrami operator of the induced metric on M. Does there exist any such surface that is of finite k-type for some integer k>2; equivalently in the paper’s terminology, can one have a decomposition x=c+x1+⋯+xk with c∈E^4 constant, each xi nonconstant, and Δxi=λi xi for k distinct real eigenvalues λ1,…,λk?
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s actual target, but it captures only the k≥3 fragment of the discussion. In §2.2 Chen first says that, based on known results, there seem to be no surfaces of k-type in S^3 for any finite k>2, and then states the broader labeled Conjecture 2 classifying all finite type surfaces in the standardly embedded S^3⊂E^4. To make the question stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the definition of finite type and k-type from §1 via the spectral decomposition of the E^4-valued immersion under the induced Laplacian. The nearby §3.1 discussion supplies the 2-type background that explains why your draft is targeting the unresolved higher-type remainder rather than the already identified 1-type and 2-type cases. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
